content.comment_body: Two questions: 1) Is it possible to send an SMS command to a standalone [product_name] communication module (without a [product_name] Basis Module) to receive its current DI/DO values? I need 0 or 1 feedback, which I can use as a variable in another [product_name] program. 2) Is it possible for a standalone [product_name] communication module to periodically send messages with DI/DO states? Thanks in advance for any assistance.

Hello [user_name], You can find application examples for using the [product_name] communication module in standalone mode (without a [product_name] Basis Module) in the Operating Instructions manual. [url] One relevant example is attached below. Hope this helps, [user_name]

You can control the two outputs of the [product_name] communication module via SMS and receive feedback about their status by SMS. However, you cannot use these feedback signals directly as VM for a [product_name] program.
Thanks for the information, [user_name]. However, I've already checked those instructions and couldn't find anything matching my requirements.
It seems attaching a [product_name] Basis Module to the communication module is necessary in this case.
If you want to use VM functionality, you need the [product_name] Basis Module attached. The standalone communication module does not support VM.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is trying to access and use real-time DI/DO values from a standalone [product_name] communication module via SMS, but discovers that while SMS feedback about outputs is possible, integrating these values into the Variable Memory area for other [product_name] applications is not supported unless a [product_name] Basis Module is attached. This is a limitation of the communication module when used independently.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects the standalone [product_name] communication module to send DI/DO statuses via SMS in a form that can be used as variables in other [product_name] applications, ideally without needing a [product_name] Basis Module attached.
